findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The change keeps the raw SHA-256 check and adds an optional semantic digest (`skill_sha256`). The digest is the parsed YAML metadata with keys sorted, plus the body bytes exactly as written. It is computed and checked by one helper (`claudeSkillSha256` / `claudeAssetMatches`) in generation, the dispatcher and status. Only exposed `skills/*/SKILL.md` files can match this way: the path regex keeps `templates/skills/...`, runtime files and other resources byte-exact. Older inventories without the field stay strict. Bad input fails closed: invalid UTF-8, missing delimiters, duplicate keys, aliases, unknown tags, non-string keys, NaN/Inf and non-map documents all throw. The dispatcher (`verifyPlugin`) and status (`observeInstalledPlugin`) catch these errors and report a damaged or errored plugin. The tests are discriminating: the positive dispatcher test asserts the normalized bytes differ from the original, so it could not pass on the raw hash alone. It also asserts that execution proof is recorded through the real bundled dispatcher. The rejection cases (metadata, body, runtime mutations, plus whitespace and CRLF changes in the body) fail with an integrity error, through both the dispatcher and the public status view. I found no regression or trust-boundary failure that blocks release.

`canonicalValue` sorts metadata keys with `String.prototype.localeCompare`, whose ordering depends on the ICU locale. The digest is computed at build time and checked on the user's machine. If the two locales order a key pair differently (for example mixed-case keys), the semantic match fails and hooks are disabled again (fail-closed, not a bypass). Current keys are lowercase ASCII, so it is not triggered today. Code-unit comparison (`left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0`) would make the digest locale-independent.

Equivalence is defined by the `yaml` package's YAML 1.2 core schema, not by the front-matter parser Claude itself uses. Some rewrites look the same to the core schema but may not to Claude's parser, e.g. a quoted value becoming a plain timestamp-like value. If Claude's parser differs (e.g. js-yaml's default schema), such a rewrite would pass integrity while changing what Claude reads. The stated threat model is accidental cache corruption, and anyone who can write the cache can already rewrite `inventory.json` and `identity.json`, so this is not a security boundary. Consider documenting the assumption or restricting accepted scalars to plain strings, booleans and arrays.

The tests and the ticket model desktop sync as `yaml.stringify(parse(header), { lineWidth: 0 })` with the body left untouched. If the real sync (#6004) also changes the blank line after the closing `---`, or adds a BOM, the skill will still be rejected and hooks will stay off. A captured real-world sample would make the RED/GREEN proof stronger than this assumed transform.

`asset-integrity.ts` pulls the `yaml` library into the bundled `runtime/dispatch.js`, which runs on every hook. That is a modest startup-cost increase on every Claude hook invocation. It is acceptable, but worth watching if hook latency matters.
